title: A failed dev-publish job leaves no comment on the issue for a pull request outcome

repository.name: workflows
repository.description: Shared, framework-agnostic GitHub-native AI workflows for the becloud-dev org

body:
A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions: 'Post the findings' runs only for draft or comment outcomes, and it runs in the rounds job before publication. If `dev-publish` fails for `action=pr` (the bundle is refused, the token cannot be minted, the push is rejected or `gh pr create` fails), no step reports it on the issue. The owner who approved the run sees neither a pull request nor a comment.

Location: .github/workflows/dev-execute.yml:293

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6145428874

<!-- release-review-finding:3:d146b252003ff4b4 -->

title: The publish scope check trusts a plan comment the rounds job can post or edit as github-actions[bot]

repository.name: workflows
repository.description: Shared, framework-agnostic GitHub-native AI workflows for the becloud-dev org

body:
A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures: 'Check the bundle against the plan' takes the last `<!-- dev-plan -->` comment by github-actions[bot], with no check against when the owner wrote `/approve`. The rounds job holds `github.token` with issues: write, and that token posts as github-actions[bot]. Round code that sets BASH_ENV through GITHUB_ENV runs inside later bash steps that have the token, such as 'Post the findings' (GH_TOKEN, draft path) or the next round's steps. From there it can add or edit a plan comment whose Files list names `.github/workflows/`, and publish then pushes an unplanned workflow with workflows write. The owner accepted this as a known gap for 0.2.0, to be fixed with the executor redesign in the next release; it matters because it defeats the control #64 adds. Accept only a plan comment created and last updated before the approval comment (`github.event.comment.created_at`), or pin the comment id and updated_at that the gate read.
Location: .github/workflows/dev-execute.yml:343

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6145787411

<!-- release-review-finding:3:e8ecff4504d3c8dd -->

title: No test pins that the push and PR steps ignore environment injected by the rounds

repository.name: workflows
repository.description: Shared, framework-agnostic GitHub-native AI workflows for the becloud-dev org

body:
The new push cases cover planted hooks, core.hooksPath, url.insteadOf and uploadpack hooks in .git. No case writes BASH_ENV or a PATH entry through GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH during a round and then asserts that the token-holding steps do not run it. Without such a case, a fix for the blocking finding could regress unnoticed.
Location: tests/dev-execute/run.sh:149

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6144852674

<!-- release-review-finding:3:d43394f0f4ce808f -->

title: No test pins that the push step ignores git hooks and config from the round's workspace

repository.name: workflows
repository.description: Shared, framework-agnostic GitHub-native AI workflows for the becloud-dev org

body:
The dev-execute suite checks permissions and stage rows, but no case plants a `.git/hooks/pre-push` or a `core.hooksPath` before the push step and asserts that it is not run. Without such a case, the fix for the token-theft path can regress unnoticed.
Location: tests/dev-execute/run.sh:1

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6135078228

title: Pass the executor App inputs from the callers before 0.2.0 moves v0

repository.name: workflows
repository.description: Shared, framework-agnostic GitHub-native AI workflows for the becloud-dev org

body:
The reusable `dev-execute.yml` on `main` requires the input `executor_app_client_id` and the secret
`executor_app_private_key`. The tag `v0` (`0712943`) has neither. Release 0.2.0 moves `v0` to a
workflow that requires them.

Neither caller passes them:
- `aif-c01-study/.github/workflows/dev-execute.yml` calls `@v0`: it breaks when `v0` moves.
- `triage-sandbox/.github/workflows/dev-execute.yml` calls `@main`: it is already incompatible.

The secrets and the client ID are granted to `aif-c01-study` at the organisation level, but the caller does not forward them.

Done when:
1. Both callers pass `executor_app_client_id` and `executor_app_private_key`.
2. A `/approve` on a `RELEASE` issue in each repository gets through the "Mint the executor App token" step.
3. The release notes for 0.2.0 name the new required input and secret, so any other caller knows.

title: Pass the round's base commit to the publish job so a merge during a round does not fail the publish

repository.name: workflows
repository.description: Shared, framework-agnostic GitHub-native AI workflows for the becloud-dev org

body:
`dev-publish` (added in #58) checks out the caller repository's default branch as it is when the job
starts, takes `git rev-parse HEAD` as the base, and requires the bundle to extend it
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" refs/push/head`). The rounds job knows the base it branched
from (`echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`) but does not pass it on: its outputs are `action`,
`verdict`, `rounds`, `branch`, `ctype` and `plan_url`.

When anything is merged to the default branch while the rounds run (they take minutes), the publish
job's base is newer than the bundle's, the check fails and no pull request is opened. It fails
closed, so nothing unsafe is pushed, but the round's work is lost until the executor is run again.

Not reproduced; found by reading the workflow on `main` at `73676d2`.

Done when:
1. The rounds job exposes the base commit it started from as a job output.
2. `dev-publish` checks out that commit and compares the bundle with it.
3. A test covers the default branch moving between the rounds and the publish: the pull request is
   still opened.
